issues.reason: Core patterns' sealing rule projects only a DEFINITE referent's Member/Name typing atom out of a seal, and 'a one-day special session' is indefinite — so its witness, typing and its reduced-relative modifier all stay sealed exactly as the instruction set directs, and nothing emitted is false, ill-typed or over-asserted.

gaps_confirmed: multi-word office title of the form noun + of-PP ('Speaker of the House') — Compound concepts covers only verb_object, phrasal verb and modifier_noun, so neither the fusion nor a genus/of-argument decomposition is specified

speaker-asserted background hung on an indefinite inside a seal: the projection rule keys on the determiner only, so the reduced relative 'being held today in Tallahassee' is sealed with its host and asserted nowhere

passive raising 'X is expected to V' with an action infinitive — Impersonal reported attitudes is written for 'to be P' small clauses while the control-verb rule bars sealing a to-infinitive; the two routes point opposite ways
new_gaps: a possessed office title predicated of a person ('Florida's Speaker of the House Johnnie Byrd') — nothing states whether the genitive attaches to the office or to the holder, and Possession is the only head available for it

a bare pre-nominal title NP as an appositive ('Speaker of the House Johnnie Byrd') — the appositive rule is stated for the comma form ('Halvard, a wheelwright'), so the tense wrapper for a pre-nominal title is unspecified
notes: The reviewer's own second gap concedes that the determiner-keyed projection rule produces exactly this sealing, so the complaint is a coverage gap, not a parse defect. Under-assertion inside a seal is the safe side of the calibration line; asserting the introduce/hold events at top level would have been the over-assertion.
